name: gpu-generated-same-node-work

protocol.note: gpu-cull-compact's atomic-append output slot order reflects GPU thread arrival order, not instance index order -- it is compared against cpu-cull-oracle as a sorted multiset of ids, never by position. vg-task-tier1-indirect's dispatch dims (TaskRecord.x/y/z) are GPU-authored from the Tier0 publication buffer and blitted straight into the indirect-args buffer within one command buffer; last_tier1_indirect_dims() is a debug/test-only readback used purely to verify the blit copied the right bytes, not a host round trip the dispatch itself depends on.

correctness.tolerance: exact (as sorted multiset for gpu-cull-compact; byte-exact, in dispatch order, for vg-task-tier1-indirect dims)

judgement: VG Task Tier1 dispatches each published task's real x/y/z dims without any host read of those dims before the indirect dispatch runs (ADR-026); the LoweringReport carries a tier1_indirect_dispatch event with real CPU encode/submit timing (TASK-B12), and has_hidden_host_wait() reports no hidden host wait was introduced by this path. GPU cull/compact demonstrates GPU-authored, atomically-claimed stream compaction whose id set matches the CPU oracle exactly once compared as a set. A follow-on million-instance harness (vertical-slice.metal.cull-compact-1m) repeats that set comparison at N=1e6 and records host wall-clock only; it does not invent gpu_ns and is not the catalog's four-variant comparative CPU-frame-time benchmark (cpu-cull+commands vs. gpu-cull+readback+CPU vs. gpu-cull+indirect vs. VG Tier1). Tier1's re-dispatch is only exercised against an idempotent (load/store-only) probe module; combining it with atomic_add is out of scope for this milestone (ADR-026 Revisit trigger).
vulkan_status: compile-review-only (ADR-024); Tier1 reuses the already-implemented dispatch_task_ring_and_tier1 (ADR-022); cull_compact_vulkan_source() exists as a GLSL analogue but is deliberately not wired into vulkan_device_hal.cpp in this milestone
